newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-U.S. BEAT NEW ZEALAND TO WIN DUNHILL CUP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-U.S. BEAT NEW ZEALAND TO WIN DUNHILL CUP.

text.p: The United States subdued a stubborn New Zealand side 2-1 to become the first three-time winners of the Alfred Dunhill Cup team golf title on Sunday.

Victories by Phil Mickelson and Steve Stricker, unbeaten throughout the tournament, offset a 69-72 defeat for Mark O'Meara by Frank Nobilo as the top-seeded U.S. trio added to their victories in 1989 and 1993.

In the key match, Mickelson moved from one shot in front to three ahead of Greg Turner when he birdied the tough 16th hole with a superb approach to four feet as Turner took bogey. He went on to win 69-72.

Stricker, unbeaten in his five matches this week, seized control against Grant Waite when he birdied the ninth, 10th and 12th holes on the way to a 67-73 triumph. It was Waite's first defeat in five matches.
In the semifinals earlier on Sunday, the U.S. trio beat unseeded Sweden 2-1 despite defeat for Mickelson in an ill-tempered match with Jarmo Sandelin.
The Americans won the tie 2-1. New Zealand, seeded seventh, upset third-seeded South Africa by the same score.
It was announced on Sunday that the tournament would continue for at least three more years to 1999 at its home on the Old Course at St Andrews.
The U.S. team won four of their five ties by 2-1. "We knew when we came here that it would be a difficult week for us because golf has developed into such a great worldwide game," O'Meara said.
"New Zealand came through a tough match this morning and played very solid golf against us. We feel very happy and privileged to have won the Cup this year.
"We came in with high hopes but we knew there were some truly great players against us. Steve won all five of his matches and that was incredible."
Nobilo said: "We can't be too disappointed, the way we played this week. It is a great week for New Zealand golf and we can feel proud of ourselves."
Nobilo produced a superb bunker shot at the famous 17th hole to preserve his lead, reminiscent of compatriot Michael Campbell's at the British Open here last year.
From up against the seven-foot wall of sand, Nobilo pitched his ball to 12 feet and holed the putt for par.
"It was perfect," he said.
After nine holes, two of the matches were level and Stricker led by a shot in the third. Nobilo gained control against O'Meara with three birdies in five holes on the back nine.
Stricker was also in charge following birdies at the 10th and 12th and the outcome depended on the Mickelson-Turner match.
Turner, a late replacement for Campbell in the New Zealand team, birdied the 10th and 12th but three-putted the 11th and 13th greens for bogeys.
Mickelson, who had also birdied the 10th, played par golf until his superb three-iron approach at the 16th led to a two-stroke swing when Nobilo missed from six feet.

Earlier, Mickelson had objected to Sandelin about the Swede's excessive celebrations whenever he holed putts, saying Sandelin had done the same thing when he beat Nick Price on the first playoff hole on Friday.
"That could have been handled better than it was by the Swede and I feel that our match could have been conducted with a little more sportsmanship and I was disappointed," he said.
He spoke to Sandelin about it at the 12th hole.
Sandelin won that match but Stricker and O'Meara each took theirs to put the Americans into the final.

Nobilo was beaten 69-72 by Ernie Els in their semifinal but Turner beat Retief Goosen by a shot and Waite nosed out Wayne Westner with a superb wedge shot to one foot of the pin at the third playoff hole after both players had missed the green.
